reading: The proposal rewords one open question and, on the record, changes nothing else. The Book 20 conversion question (q-conversion-settlement) no longer asks whether the conversion is a lasting settlement or a stage the finale must revisit (E5). It asks whether the conversion reaches the shares the Mill Compact purchased (E9), as the instruction requested without deciding the answer (E1). The two other examined questions are unchanged (E14, E18). Interpretation: the question's focus moves from durability over time to scope of application.

concerns.title: Book 20 conversion question: from durability to reach
concerns.earlier: Is the conversion a lasting settlement, or a stage the finale must revisit? (E5)
concerns.proposed: Does the conversion reach the shares the Mill Compact purchased, or do they stay outside it? Not decided. (E9)
concerns.reading: The same question identity is kept, but what it asks changes: from how long the conversion holds to whom it applies. The instruction asks for exactly this rewording and leaves the answer open. Interpretation: this is a change of formulation, and the record does not show whether it is also a change of meaning.
counterevidence: E9 does not say the durability question is dropped; its wording only asks about reach.
concerns.competing_reading: The reach question may be a refinement that presupposes durability is still open, not a replacement of it.

concerns.title: Durability of the Book 20 conversion
concerns.earlier: Whether the conversion is a lasting settlement or a stage the finale must revisit (E5, E8).
concerns.proposed: The proposed wording mentions neither lasting settlement nor the finale (E9).
concerns.reading: The durability formulation no longer appears in the proposed wording, and the Book 24 decision records it as the current wording of this question. Whether it still needs separate consideration, and whether its loss was intended, is not shown by the record.
counterevidence: E8 says Book 24 makes the question concrete without answering it, so Book 24 does not itself settle durability.
E6 records no earlier wording before the identity was recorded, so the question cannot be traced further back.
concerns.competing_reading: Durability may remain implicitly open under the reach question, or be carried by the finale mechanism question; the evidence does not show which.

concerns.title: Compact settlement through grain-labour
concerns.reading: The question of whether the Compact accepts grain-labour to settle its claim, and whether the Gate Table schedule reaches its lowland draw, is unchanged in wording. Book 24 records it as current without deciding it.

concerns.title: What the lowland towns and Ammen owe each other
concerns.reading: The broad question of mutual obligation between the lowland towns and Ammen is unchanged in wording and identity.

concerns.title: Overlap between conversion reach and Compact settlement
concerns.reading: The proposed wording now names the Mill Compact, as the unchanged Compact settlement question already does. Interpretation: the two questions now touch the same party, and an answer to one may bear on the other. The record does not show that they conflict.
counterevidence: E2 and E3 are interpretive or discovery material, not recorded decisions.

prospective.text: Book 24 records a decision on q-conversion-settlement, whose wording the proposal changes. This is a recorded relationship by identity, not a demonstrated contradiction. Book 24 also records the Compact grain-labour decision, unchanged.
Speculative: if the conversion is later read as reaching purchased shares, Oona's grain-labour offer in Book 24 could be read as an in-kind answer. This is not recorded anywhere.
Speculative: the Compact's Books 27-29 bid might need reconsidering if the reach question is answered either way. Book 25 was listed by title only and was not read for decisions.

alternatives.title: Keep the durability wording as recorded
alternatives.summary: Leave q-conversion-settlement as it stands and leave the Compact reach question to q-compact-settlement. Keeps the durability question and the Book 24 decision wording intact.
alternatives.gains: No wording drift; Book 24's current decision stays aligned.
alternatives.costs: The reach question in E3 stays unasked, and its consequence for lowland obligations may stay hidden.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether Book 24 and Book 25 decisions already imply an answer on reach.

alternatives.title: Hold durability and reach as two questions
alternatives.summary: Keep q-conversion-settlement on durability and keep q-compact-settlement. A distinct reach question would be described here, not given an identity. Interpretation: this is the strongest option here because it loses neither formulation and decides neither answer.
alternatives.gains: Preserves the earlier concern and the proposal's new focus together.
alternatives.costs: Adds a question to track and may overlap q-compact-settlement.
alternatives.next_investigation: Ask whether the reach question can be answered independently of the Compact grain-labour question.

alternatives.title: Treat reach, grain-labour and lowland obligation together
alternatives.summary: Read the reach of the conversion, the Compact's grain-labour settlement and the lowland obligation question as one inquiry about what lowland parties owe Ammen, as E3 suggests.
alternatives.gains: Surfaces how the answers constrain each other.
alternatives.costs: Merges three open questions and may close off independent answers; durability stays unaddressed.
alternatives.next_investigation: Test whether each question can still be answered alone after the others are fixed.

alternatives.title: Tie the conversion's reach to the finale mechanism
alternatives.summary: Ask whether the conversion's reach depends on which finale mechanism is chosen, since E2 notes it has no force under A. This reframes the proposal's question as dependent on the finale choice.
alternatives.gains: Makes the weight of the finale choice visible.
alternatives.costs: Ties a Book 20 question to an undecided finale and may delay answering it.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether Book 20 events can be written without knowing the finale mechanism.

not_established: Whether the loss of the durability wording was intended; the instruction does not name it.
Whether Book 25, listed by title only, depends on the conversion question.
Whether the conversion reaches the Compact's purchased shares; no answer is recorded.
Whether any Working Book decision conflicts with the reworded question; Book 24 is related by identity only.
Earlier history of the conversion question before revision 3; no identity was recorded (E6).
